title.en: Who runs for the school election?

text.en: Every election needs groups of people who agree on how to run things. Political parties do that job in a democracy. Let us see their functions and challenges.

A political party is a group of people who come together to contest elections and hold power in government. They agree on policies for the good of society.
Parties contest elections, put forward policies and programmes, make laws, form and run governments, play the role of opposition, shape public opinion and run welfare schemes.
A party has leaders, active members and followers. Parties are necessary because democracy needs representation and competition.
In a one-party, two-party or multi-party system, the number of parties vary. India has a multi-party system with alliances.
The Election Commission registers parties and recognises national parties. A national party must get at least six per cent of total votes in four states and win at least four seats in the Lok Sabha.
Parties face challenges like lack of internal democracy, dynastic succession, money and muscle power, and meaningless choices.
Anti-defection law and mandatory disclosure of assets and criminal cases are some reforms. Citizens can also pressure parties.
Voters are the real power. Informed voting and participation help keep parties accountable.
